data_output.description: encode(splits) remains unchanged and returns encoded[name] = (features, labels, users). users are canonical-row-order values sourced from the exact raw field user_id. Training weights are not a data.py output: train.py derives one float32 weight per encoded training row exclusively from train_users, with weight_i = (1 / training_count(user_id_i)) * (N_train / sum_j(1 / training_count(user_id_j))).

model_input.description: Model.logits and Model.predict continue to accept encoded int32 feature matrices. Model.step accepts (features, labels, sample_weights), where labels and sample_weights are aligned one-dimensional arrays of the same batch length; sample_weights are globally normalized training-only inverse-user-frequency float32 weights. Validation and test prediction calls do not receive labels or weights.

model_designer.objective: Implement weighted binary cross-entropy gradient and reporting in model.py so the trainer can apply per-training-row user-normalized loss weights.
required_changes: Change Model.step in model.py to accept a third required argument sample_weights aligned one-to-one with labels and features rows.
Validate that sample_weights is one-dimensional, has len(sample_weights) == len(labels), and is finite; raise ValueError for a violation.
Compute the per-row logit derivative as ((sigmoid(logits) - labels) * sample_weights / len(labels)).astype(np.float32). Use this derivative for both np.add.at weight gradients and the bias update.
Keep the existing L2 term exactly as self.l2 * self.weights, added once per batch after accumulating the weighted data gradient.
Return weighted BCE reported as the arithmetic mean of sample_weights * (-(labels * log(probabilities + 1e-9) + (1 - labels) * log(1 - probabilities + 1e-9))).
preserve: Preserve the additive scorer exactly: bias plus the sum of embedding weights selected by the existing encoded feature columns.
Preserve sigmoid clipping, Adam hyperparameters and state behavior, learning-rate handling, L2 behavior, prediction batching, and checkpoint state interface.
Do not add features, change data loading, alter optimizer configuration, or use validation or test labels in Model.
coordination_notes: Trainer will call model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch], train_weights[batch]) and will provide float32 weights with global training-set mean equal to one.
The weighted derivative must divide by the actual current batch length, not by sum(sample_weights), so normalized weights alter user contribution while retaining the parent batch-scale convention.
The contract-check path will also pass aligned probe weights.

trainer.objective: Implement training-only inverse-training-impression user weights in train.py and pass them to the weighted Model.step call without changing configured optimization or validation-only checkpoint selection.
required_changes: Retain the encoded training user array by changing the train unpacking to train_features, train_labels, train_users = encoded["train"].

Immediately after encoding, derive train_weights solely from train_users (which originate from the exact raw field user_id in canonical training-row order): count each distinct user_id's occurrences over the entire training split, assign every row preliminary weight 1.0 / count(train_users[row]), then multiply all preliminary weights by len(train_users) / preliminary_weights.sum(). Store the result as a one-dimensional np.float32 array. This produces mean weight exactly approximately one in float32 and equal total preliminary mass per user.
Raise ValueError if the training split is empty, if derived weights are non-finite, or if their length differs from len(train_labels).
In normal training, replace each two-argument step call with model.step(train_features[batch], train_labels[batch], train_weights[batch]).

In --contract-check mode, derive and slice the same train_weights and call model.step(train_features[:probe_size], train_labels[:probe_size], train_weights[:probe_size]). Do not use a separately recomputed probe-only user frequency.
Do not edit config.json; its seed, learning_rate, l2, batch_size, max_epochs, patience, and split values remain exactly unchanged.
preserve: Preserve the current load and encode feature pipeline, including its training-only vocabularies and canonical split row order.
Preserve shuffled row batching, configured optimizer settings, configured batch size, epoch count, seed, and patience.

Continue selecting checkpoints and early stopping solely from within_user_auc on encoded validation users, validation labels, and validation predictions. Never load, infer, inspect, or use test labels.

Preserve creation of predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz. Each must contain exactly row_ids and scores, with row_ids=np.arange for its respective encoded split and scores in canonical validation or test source row order.
coordination_notes: Model.step will require sample_weights as its third argument after model_designer's change; pass only training-derived train_weights to it.
Do not modify data.py: user_id is already carried as the third element of every encoded split tuple and is the only source required for this loss weighting.
The normalization must be global over all training rows, not separately normalized within shuffled batches, so every user has equal total loss mass across a full epoch.

reasoning: This is a loss-only ablation. It uses only the existing exact raw user_id carried from the training log, computes inverse training-impression weights exclusively from the training split, globally normalizes their mean to one, and applies them only to training BCE. Features, additive architecture, optimizer, batch size, configuration, validation proxy, validation-only checkpoint selection, and prediction artifact contract remain unchanged.
